newsitem.title: USA: Viacom loses $217 million, hurt by Blockbuster charge.
newsitem.headline: Viacom loses $217 million, hurt by Blockbuster charge.

text.p: Entertainment giant Viacom Inc. said on Tuesday it lost $217 million in the second quarter, hamstrung by a $323 million pre-tax charge in its poor-performing Blockbuster video rental business.

Excluding the Blockbuster charge, the loss was about $14 million, compared with a profit of $26 million a year ago. Viacom's revenues in the latest quarter rose to $3.03 billion from $2.79 billion, paced by double-digit growth in its MTV cable networks, Paramount movie business and Spelling Entertainment unit.
The loss, equal to 66 cents a share including the Blockbuster charge, or eight cents without the charge, compared with a profit of three cents a share a year ago.
Viacom reported second-quarter EBITDA -- or earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization -- of $127 million, versus $472 million a year ago.

In addition to the charge for store closings and writedown of excess video inventory at Blockbuster, the video chain also suffered through a poor quarterly performance. It said margins were hurt by carrying a larger retail product mix and higher costs from overbuying of videotapes.
"In the second quarter, all of Viacom's business segments, aside from Blockbuster, turned in solid performances," said Sumner Redstone, chairman and chief executive.
He said the company has "to a large extent identified the issues which contributed to its unsatisfactory (Blockbuster) performance."

New management "is putting operational and marketing initiatives in place" to refocus the business, Redstone added. "We are optimistic that Blockbuster will enter a period of renewed growth next year."

For the quarter, cash flow at its entertainment businesses, including Paramount Pictures, decreased 17 percent to $95 million due to a change in Paramount's television product mix and lower profits from feature films. Revenues rose 14 percent to $862.3 million.
Networks and broadcasting revenues increased 11 percent to $626 million, while cash flow rose 19 percent to $200 million.

Showtime networks' cash flow gained 63 percent, due in part to growth in the direct broadcast satellite industry in the United States. Showtime subscribers increased by nearly two million from a year ago to 17.1 million at June 30.

Publishing revenues, including Simon & Shuster, increased 4 percent to $535 million, while cash flow rose 6 percent to $56 million, helped by strong international sales in European, Asian and Latin-American markets.
Viacom's stock gained 62.5 cents to $30.8125 in early trading on the American Stocvk Exchange.
